reaped-status.comment: plan 311: 'the reaped status' - the raw wait4 status word from the most recent successful reap. A fixed three-word phrase with no expression inside, so it is matched as one construct. 'the reaped' followed by anything else falls through to the article + bare-identifier rules and stays an ordinary variable reference, so 'reaped' remains usable as a name.
reaped-status.name: support.function.vox

reap-no-hang.comment: plan 311: 'without waiting' - the WNOHANG suffix on a reap. Matched as a two-word phrase so 'waiting' is coloured only here, not claimed as a global keyword; it stays an ordinary identifier everywhere else (the spec requires this). 'without' alone is already an action keyword for 'print ... without newline'; this lifts the pair to a control modifier when they appear together.
reap-no-hang.name: keyword.control.vox

function-definition.comment: Function definition: To <name>. Names are bare or single-quoted identifiers (double quotes are string literals, never names).

function-call.comment: Function call in expression position: 'add up' of 3. Only the quoted form is matched here, so bare element-access like 'element N of list' is not mis-coloured as a call.

patterns.comment: Character literal: exactly one char between single quotes ('A'). A one-character quoted token is never a name.
patterns.name: constant.character.vox

patterns.comment: Possessive marker on a bare name: person's length. Must run BEFORE the quoted-identifier rule, or its greedy [^']+ would swallow from this apostrophe to the next single quote anywhere later in the line.
patterns.name: punctuation.accessor.vox

patterns.comment: Quoted identifier (two or more chars): 'multi word'. An immediately-following possessive s ('name's length) is captured as the accessor so it does not render as plain text.

types.comment: Type names (storage.type): Number, Float, Int, Text, Boolean, List, Map, Buffer, File, Bytes, Byte and their aliases.
types.name: storage.type.vox

null-literal.comment: The nothing/null/nil value literal (distinct from the 'empty' property predicate).
null-literal.name: constant.language.null.vox

loop-expansion.comment: Parameter loop expansion: 'each X from Y' - uses entity.name.tag for distinct blue color
loop-expansion.name: entity.name.tag.each.vox

conditional-branch.comment: Conditional branching: 'but' keyword - uses support.type for distinct teal/cyan color
conditional-branch.name: support.type.vox

import-keywords.comment: Library/import keywords: see, library, version (stray occurrences; the library-declaration and see-import patterns colour them in context).
import-keywords.name: keyword.control.import.vox

argument-keywords.comment: Arguments and environment: argument(s), environment, variable, count, raw and their aliases.
argument-keywords.name: keyword.other.vox

io-keywords.comment: File I/O actions and stream modes.
io-keywords.name: support.function.vox

time-keywords.comment: Time and timer keywords: wait/sleep/get, current time, durations and units.
time-keywords.name: keyword.other.vox

operators.comment: Arithmetic, comparison, logical, cast and bitwise operators. The bit-* forms are listed first so they match as a whole before their inner 'and'/'or'/'not'.
operators.name: keyword.operator.vox

property-keywords.comment: Standalone property/predicate keywords (reserved words, always the keyword): 'is empty', 'is zero', 'of size 16', etc.
property-keywords.name: variable.other.property.vox

properties.comment: Possessive property access: X's capacity / X's first / X's all / X's count.

articles.comment: Grammatical particles and range markers (articles, prepositions, collection quantifiers) - muted so they do not compete with real keywords. Lexer groups these as Range/Collection.
articles.name: punctuation.definition.vox

function-call-bare.comment: Bare function call in expression position: addup of 3. Runs AFTER every keyword rule, so the only bare words that reach it are identifiers — keywords (element, byte, first, length, ...) are already consumed. The negative lookbehind still guards the two element-access idioms whose INDEX is a bare identifier: 'element N of list' and 'byte i of buffer'. Without it, N/i would be mis-coloured as a function call. Placed before #bare-identifier so a real callee takes the function-call scope, not the variable scope.

bare-identifier.comment: Catch-all for bare identifiers (variables, bare callees without of/on, indices): total in 'called total', addup in 'print addup.', N in 'element N of list'. Runs LAST so every lexer keyword (the grammar covers all of them — check-grammar.sh enforces 0 missing) is matched by its own rule first; only leftover bare words are identifiers. This is what makes the common case — bare names, 767 of 788 after migration — render as names instead of grey, matching the quoted form's variable.other.vox scope.
bare-identifier.name: variable.other.vox
